Rashi on Berakhot 45b:10:1.hebrew: לאו דשמיע להו מרבי יוחנן - דבר מערבא הוא, דאילו רב בבבל הוה, ובני מערבא היכא שמיע להו:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:10:1.english: Is it not that they heard it from Rabbi Yoḥanan - For [Rabbi Yoḥanan] was a resident of the West [Eretz Yisrael], whereas Rav was in Babylonia, and where would the people of the West have heard it [from Rav]?

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:11:1.hebrew: והוא דקרו ליה ועני - שסמוך הוא אצלם, ועונה ברוך הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:11:1.english: And that is when they call him and he answers - That he is close to them, and he answers, "Blessed is He."

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:12:1.hebrew: לא אמרן - דלא צריך למיתי גבייהו אלא שלשה, אבל עשרה שיצטרפו משום הזכרת השם — עד דאתי גבייהו:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:12:1.english: We only said [this] - That he does not need to come to them [applies] only to three; but [regarding] ten, who join together on account of the mention of the [Divine] Name — [they cannot do so] until he comes to them.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:13:1.hebrew: נראין כעשרה - דאין אדם ממהר להבחין בין עשרה לתשעה:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:13:1.english: They appear like ten - For a person does not quickly distinguish between ten and nine.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:15:1.hebrew: מצוה ליחלק - ולברך כל אחד בפני עצמו — בין ברכת המוציא, בין ברכת המזון:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:15:1.english: It is a mitzva to separate - And for each one to recite the blessing for himself — whether the blessing of HaMotzi or the Grace after Meals.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:16:1.hebrew: אחד מפסיק לשנים - אם גמרו השנים סעודתן ורוצין לזמן, דרך ארץ הוא שיהא האחד מפסיק את סעודתו עד שיזמנו עליו, עד ברכת הזן — דהיינו ברכת זימון — וחוזר וגומר סעודתו. אבל שנים, אין עליהם להפסיק בשביל היחיד, וימתין עד שיגמרו:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:16:1.english: One interrupts for two - If the two finished their meal and wish to recite the zimmun, it is proper etiquette that the one interrupt his meal until they recite the zimmun with him, until [the conclusion of] Birkat HaZan — that is, the zimmun blessing — and then he resumes and finishes his meal. But two are not obligated to interrupt for the sake of the individual, and he [the individual] must wait until they finish.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:17:1.english: Beyond the letter of the law - To accord him importance.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:18:1.hebrew: לא הוה בהו - מופלג בחכמה ובזקנה מן השנים:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:18:1.english: There was not among them - [One who was] distinguished in wisdom and in age from the [other] two.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:18:2.hebrew: דאיכא אדם גדול - שהגדול מברך, כדפסקינן לקמן הלכתא (דף מז.):
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:18:2.english: Where there is a great man - For the greatest [one] recites the blessing, as we rule below as the halakha (page 47a).

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:1:1.hebrew: דניחא להו דמקבע להו בחובה - דגדול המצווה ועושה:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:1:1.english: That they prefer to be established under an obligation - For greater is one who is commanded and performs [than one who is not commanded and performs].

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:20:1.english: [One who] came and found them - One from the street came and found three who were reciting the zimmun.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:20:2.english: Blessed and blessed - For he cannot say, "that we have eaten of His [food]."

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:21:1.hebrew: הא דקאמר ברוך ומבורך - כדאשכחינהו דקאמר המזמן נברך, אבל אשכחינהו דענו ברוך — הוא עונה בתרייהו אמן:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:21:1.english: This [case] where he says, "Blessed and praised" - [This is] when he found them as the leader [of the zimmun] says, "Let us bless." But [if] he found them when they answered, "Blessed," he answers "Amen" after them.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:23:1.hebrew: הא בבונה ירושלים - שהיא סוף הברכות, הרי זה משובח. וכן בסוף ברכות דקריאת שמע, שחרית וערבית. ואחר כל ברכותיו דקתני בברייתא הרי זה משובח — אחר גמר כל ברכותיו קאמר. ואחר כל ברכותיו דקתני הרי זה מגונה — בסוף כל ברכה וברכה קאמר:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:23:1.english: This is in [the blessing] "Who builds Jerusalem" - As it is the end of the blessings, [answering amen] is praiseworthy. And likewise at the end of the blessings of the recitation of the Shema, [both] morning and evening. And [as for] "after all his blessings" that is taught in the baraita, "it is praiseworthy" — it means after the completion of all his blessings. And [as for] "after all his blessings" that is taught, "it is reprehensible" — it means at the end of each and every blessing.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:24:1.hebrew: כי היכי דלשמעו פועלים - וידעו שנגמרה כל הברכה, שהרי אין המברך עונה אמן אלא לבסוף:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:24:1.english: So that the workers would hear - And [they] would know that the entire blessing has concluded, for the one reciting the blessing answers 'amen' only at the end.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:24:2.hebrew: וליקומו - לעבידתייהו. ואי משום דקמפקע להו מהטוב והמטיב — לא איכפת ליה, דקסבר דלאו דאורייתא היא, אלא ביבנה תקנוה על הרוגי ביתר שנתנו לקבורה:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:24:2.english: And get up - To their work. And if [it is] because he releases them from [the blessing of] "HaTov VeHaMeitiv" — he was not concerned, for he held that it is not from the Torah, but rather they instituted it in Yavneh concerning the slain of Beitar, who were given over for burial.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:24:3.hebrew: רב אשי עני - לההוא אמן בלחישה, כי היכי דלא לשמעו וידעו ששם גמר הברכות ויזלזלו בהטוב והמטיב. ומיהו, משום דסוף כל ברכותיו היה, ותניא בברייתא ה"ז משובח, לא סגי דלא עני ליה:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:24:3.english: Rav Ashi answered - [He answered] that amen in a whisper, so that they would not hear and know that the conclusion of the blessings is there, and treat [the blessing of] HaTov VeHaMeitiv lightly. However, since it was the end of all his blessings, and it is taught in a baraita, "This is praiseworthy," he could not refrain from answering it.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:2:1.hebrew: אם רצו אין מזמנים - כדמפרש טעמא לקמן, שאין קביעותן נאה משום פריצותא — בין דנשים, בין דמשכב זכור דעבדים בקטנים:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:2:1.english: If they wish, they may not form a zimmun - As [the Gemara] explains the reason below, that their establishing [a meal together] is not seemly due to licentiousness — whether [that] of women, or [that] of homosexual intercourse of slaves with minors.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:2:2.hebrew: דאפילו מאה כתרי דמיין - לענין חובה, דאין חייבות לזמן, ואם רצו מזמנין. והוא הדין לשנים:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:2:2.english: That even a hundred are considered like two - In regard to obligation: that they are not obligated to form a zimmun, but if they wish, they may form a zimmun. And the same applies to two [men].

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:3:1.hebrew: דאיכא דעות - דאע"ג דלענין חובה אינן חייבות, לענין רשות דעות שלשה חשיבי להודות טפי משני אנשים, דאיכא משום גדלו לה' אתי:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:3:1.english: Because there are minds - For even though with regard to an obligation they [women] are not obligated, with regard to an optional [zimmun], the minds of three [people] are considered more significant for giving thanks than two men, as there is [the verse], "Magnify the Lord with me."

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:6:1.hebrew: קוראין לו - להודיעו שהם רוצים לזמן, ויפנה אליהם במקום מעמדו, ודי להם בכך:
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:6:1.english: They call him - To inform him that they want to form a zimmun, and [so that] he will turn toward them where he is standing; and that is sufficient for them.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:6:2.english: And they include him in the zimmun - Even though he does not come to them.

Rashi on Berakhot 45b:9:1.hebrew: ואמר רבי זירא לומר שאין ברכת הזימון ביניהן - לא בא ללמדנו אלא שאין צריכין זימון. דכיון דאחד יוצא בברכת חברו, אשמעינן דאין זימון; דאי יש זימון — ברכת שניהם היא, שהרי אומר "נברך" והוא עונה "ברוך הוא":
Rashi on Berakhot 45b:9:1.english: And Rabbi Zeira said: To say that there is no blessing of zimmun between them - [Rabbi Yoḥanan] came only to teach us that they do not require zimmun. For since [he states that] one fulfills [his obligation] through his fellow's blessing, he teaches us that there is no zimmun; for if there were zimmun, it would be the blessing of both of them, since [one] says "Let us bless" and he answers "Blessed is He".

Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:20:1.hebrew: רב זביד אמר ברוך הוא ומבורך - ובה"ג פסק: "ברוך הוא ומבורך שמו תמיד לעולם ועד". ואי הוה עשרה, עני בתרייהו: "ברוך הוא אלהינו ומבורך שמו תמיד לעולם ועד":
Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:20:1.english: Rav Zevid said: "Blessed is He and blessed" - And in the Halakhot Gedolot, he ruled: "Blessed is He and blessed is His Name continually, forever and ever." And if there were ten, he answers after them: "Blessed is He, our God, and blessed is His Name continually, forever and ever."

Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:23:1.hebrew: הא בבונה ירושלים הא בשאר ברכות - פר"ח וה"ג: די"מ בכל ברכה וברכה, כגון אחר ישתבח וכיוצא בו. ומיהו, פוק חזי מאי עמא דבר — שלא נהגו לענות אמן אלא אחר בונה ירושלים דבהמ"ז:
Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:23:1.english: "This is in 'Who builds Jerusalem'; this is in other blessings" - Rabbeinu Chananel and the Halakhot Gedolot explained that some explain [that answering amen applies] to each and every blessing [that concludes a sequence], such as after Yishtabach and the like. However, go out and see what the people do — for they are not accustomed to answer amen except after "Who builds Jerusalem" in the Grace after Meals.

Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:24:1.hebrew: רב אשי עני ליה בלחישה - וכן פסק בה"ג. ועוד, לדידן דליכא פועלים — אפילו אביי מודה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:24:1.english: "Rav Ashi would answer it in a whisper" - And so ruled the author of Halakhot Gedolot. And furthermore, in our case, where there are no workers, even Abaye concedes [that one should answer in a whisper].

Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:2:1.hebrew: והא מאה נשי כתרי גברי דמיין - לענין קבוץ תפלה ולענין כל דבר שבעשרה, ואפילו הכי חשבינן להו כשלשה, וה"ה לשנים. אבל לא מצי למימר "כחד דמיין" — דאינן יכולות לזמן, דהא קתני: "נשים מזמנות לעצמן". ורש"י פירש: "כתרי" — לענין חובה, דאין חייבות לזמן, ואם רצו מזמנות, והוא הדין לשנים:
Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:2:1.english: "And aren't one hundred women considered like two men?" - [That is,] with regard to gathering for prayer and with regard to any matter requiring ten; and even so, we consider them like three [to form a zimmun], and the same applies to two [men]. But [the Gemara] could not say "they are considered like one [man]" — [which would imply] that they cannot form a zimmun — for it teaches: "Women form a zimmun for themselves." And Rashi explained: "Like two" [means] with regard to obligation — for they are not obligated to form a zimmun, but if they wish, they may form a zimmun; and the same applies to two [men].

Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:3:1.hebrew: שאני התם דאיכא דעות - מכאן משמע דנשים יכולות לזמן לעצמן, וכן עשו בנות רבינו אברהם חמיו של רבינו יהודה ע"פ אביהן. ומיהו לא נהגו העולם כן. וקשה: אמאי לא נהגו? מדקתני "מזמנות" — משמע דקאמר חייבות לזמן! וי"ל, ד"נשים מזמנות לעצמן" היינו: אם רצו לזמן — מזמנות. וכן משמע קצת הלשון, מדקתני בסמוך: "נשים ועבדים אם רצו לזמן אין מזמנין". ועוד, דמדמה ליה הגמרא לשנים, משמע דחובה ליכא. והא דקאמר בריש ערכין (דף ג. ושם): "הכל מחוייבין בזימון לאתויי נשים" — לענין רשות קאמר, ולא לענין חובה. ונשים — צריך עיון אם יוצאות בברכת הזימון של אנשים, מאחר שאין מבינות. ויש מביאין ראיה שיוצאות, מדאמר לקמן: "סופר מברך ובור יוצא"; מכאן משמע שאף הנשים יוצאות בבהמ"ז שלנו. מיהו יש לדחות אותה ראיה: דשאני בור שמבין בלשון הקדש ויודע קצת מאי קאמר, אבל אינו יודע לברך; אבל נשים, שאינן מבינות כלל, מצי למימר דלא נפקי. והא דאמרי' במגילה (פ"ב ד' יז.): "לועז ששמע אשורית יצא" — פרסומי ניסא בעלמא שאני, כדאמרינן התם (דף יח.): "האחשתרנים בני הרמכים", מי ידעינן מאי ניהו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:3:1.english: "There it is different, because there are [separate] minds" - From here it implies that women may form a zimmun for themselves, and so did the daughters of Rabbeinu Avraham, the father-in-law of Rabbeinu Yehudah, based on [the ruling of] their father. However, people are not accustomed to do so. And it is difficult: Why are they not accustomed [to do so]? For from that which it teaches: "they form a zimmun," it implies that it means they are obligated to form a zimmun! And one can say that "women form a zimmun for themselves" means: if they wish to form a zimmun, they may form a zimmun. And the wording somewhat implies this as well, from that which it teaches adjacent [to this]: "Women and slaves, if they wish to form a zimmun, they may not form a zimmun." And furthermore, since the Gemara compares it to two [men], it implies that there is no obligation. And as for that which [the Gemara] says at the beginning of Arakhin (3a and there): "'All are obligated in zimmun' — to include women" — it is stated regarding permission, and not regarding an obligation. And [regarding] women, it requires investigation whether they fulfill their obligation through the zimmun blessing of men, since they do not understand [Hebrew]. And some bring proof that they fulfill [their obligation], from that which [the Gemara] states below: "A scribe recites the blessing and an unlearned person fulfills [his obligation]"; from here it implies that even women fulfill [their obligation] in our Grace after Meals. However, one can reject that proof: for an unlearned person is different, as he understands the Holy Tongue and knows somewhat what [the leader] is saying, but he does not know [how] to recite the blessing [himself]; but [regarding] women, who do not understand at all, one can say that they do not fulfill [their obligation]. And as for that which we say in Megillah (chapter 2, 17a): "A foreign speaker who heard [the Megillah read in] Ashurit has fulfilled [his obligation]" — merely publicizing the miracle is different, as we say there (18a): "'Ha'achashteranim bnei haramachim' [Esther 8:10] — do we know what they are?!"

Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:4:1.hebrew: אי הכי אימא סיפא - לא גרס "אי הכי", דהא אפי' מעיקר' נמי הוה מצי למפרך מסיפא: דאין מזמנין:
Tosafot on Berakhot 45b:4:1.english: "If so, say the latter clause" - One does not read "If so," for even from the outset, [the Gemara] could also have objected from the latter clause: that they may not form a zimmun.
